draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Murud-Janjira! This island fort just off the town of Murud let the Siddis hold out against the Marathas, the Mughals and the Portuguese, none of whom ever managed to take it.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named place to eat in my notes for Murud, so ask around town for the day's fresh catch.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The fort itself is right here, sitting on its island just off Murud's coast.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a spot on the Murud shore and look out at the fort's walls rising from the water.
moodReplies.surprise-me: In 1682 Sambhaji teamed up with Prince Akbar, Aurangzeb's rebel son, to besiege Janjira, and even then the fort didn't fall.

spots.name: Murud-Janjira
spots.detail: 1 min walk · The island fort that held off every siege

tips.title: Plan for the crossing.
tips.body: The fort stands on an island just off Murud, so leave time to get across and back.

tips.title: Go in daylight.
tips.body: You'll want good light to explore the walls and take in the sea views.

story.title: A fort on the island
story.body: Janjira Fort was built off the coast of Murud, with Malik Ambar credited for its construction. It became the stronghold of the Siddis.

story.title: Allies of the Mughals
story.body: After the Ahmadnagar Sultanate fell, the Siddis of Janjira allied with the Mughal Empire. They were a constant threat to the Marathas of the Konkan.

story.title: Attempts that failed
story.body: Shivaji made several attempts to capture Janjira, the Siddi capital. Every one of them failed.

story.title: Sambhaji's siege
story.body: Sambhaji besieged the fort with help from Prince Akbar and the Rajputs of Marwar. Mughal attacks on the Konkan pulled him away, and the Siddis chased the retreating Marathas.
